title: Lab / Bench Work Physical Attendance Parameter
content: When a JD mentions lab environment, bench work, hardware bring-up, testing with physical equipment, or oscilloscope usage, a non-conventional 'Lab/Bench Work Required' parameter must be derived. This parameter requires candidates to demonstrate physical lab access and hands-on hardware experience. Remote-only candidates who cannot be on-site for lab sessions are incompatible with this parameter unless the JD explicitly states remote lab access is supported.

title: Travel Requirement Parameter
content: When a JD explicitly mentions travel (e.g., 'travel up to 25%', 'client site visits', 'international travel required'), a 'Travel Required' non-conventional parameter must be derived. Evaluate candidates for: history of roles involving client travel, consultant or professional services backgrounds, and willingness statements (if available in cover letters). Do not assume travel willingness from country-of-residence alone.

title: Startup Fit / Fast-Paced Environment Parameter
content: When a JD uses startup signals such as 'fast-paced environment', 'wear many hats', 'ambiguity', 'high ownership', 'scrappy team', 'zero-to-one', this triggers a 'Startup Fit' non-conventional parameter. Evaluate candidates for: history at early-stage companies (<100 employees), demonstrated breadth across multiple technical domains, ownership of complete product surfaces, and evidence of adapting to rapidly changing priorities. Large enterprise-only backgrounds may be flagged for this parameter.

title: Client-Facing Ownership Parameter
content: When a JD mentions direct client interaction, customer-facing responsibilities, external stakeholder management, or customer success involvement, a 'Client-Facing Ownership' non-conventional parameter applies. Evidence to evaluate: described external client or customer interaction in prior roles, presentations or demos to non-technical stakeholders, escalation handling experience, and ability to translate technical context for business audiences.

title: On-Call / Shift Work Parameter
content: When a JD specifies on-call rotations, shift work, 24/7 support responsibilities, or after-hours availability, a 'On-Call/Shift' non-conventional parameter must be derived. Evidence includes: SRE or DevOps roles with described on-call rotation participation, described incident response involvement outside business hours, or operational roles with defined shift structures. This parameter should not be scored — flag as 'unscored_if: candidate has not described on-call or shift availability'.
